qa.question: What are the C2 indicators for this infection?
qa.answer: Domain vadusa.xyz resolves to 45.131.214.85. The infected host queried vadusa.xyz at 19:55:51 UTC and, within the same second, opened a TCP session to 45.131.214.85:443 that stayed open for the rest of the capture (~4.3 hours). Despite using port 443, the session is plaintext HTTP, not TLS -- 273 requests of the form 'POST http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1' with header 'User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3', answered with 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' / 'Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.92 (Windows NT)' and an encoded 'CMD=ENCD' body. This directly confirms NetSupport Manager RAT C2 traffic, disguised on port 443 to blend in with HTTPS but not actually encrypted with TLS.
qa.evidence: http.log.json requests/responses on the 10.2.28.88:51912 <-> 45.131.214.85:443 flow (literal User-Agent/Server headers); dns.log.json (A record vadusa.xyz -> 45.131.214.85); conn.log.json for session duration/packet counts. Note: this was initially missed by an early version of this pipeline's HTTP parser, which assumed CRLF line endings -- NetSupport's HTTP implementation uses bare LF, which silently produced empty Host/User-Agent fields until fixed and re-verified against the raw packet bytes.
